t: This is King Edward Street, in the City of London, running from Newgate Street in the south up to Little Britain in the north. Postman's Park lies along its east side. The street is named after Edward the Sixth, who became king of England and Ireland in 1547 at the age of nine. He was the first English monarch raised as a Protestant, and because he died before reaching maturity, a regency council governed in his name for the whole of his reign.
